content: A critical factor directly influencing toll processing demand is the operational status of coal washeries. Washeries are essential components of the coal supply chain, responsible for removing impurities and preparing raw coal for end-use markets. The availability of these facilities dictates the flow of processed coal, meaning that any closures or maintenance shutdowns directly impact supply cycles. When washeries go offline, the availability of processed coal is reduced, which tightens supply and potentially drives up market prices. Historical data reflecting washery closures and maintenance shutdowns demonstrates a direct and measurable correlation with the toll processing demand index. An analysis of the operational cycles between 2024 and 2025 reveals an overall decreasing trend in both downtime and processing demand metrics. Specifically, closures and maintenance shutdowns reached a maximum value of 60.0 days in 2024 before declining significantly to a minimum value of 30.0 days in 2025. Concurrently, the Toll Processing Demand Index exhibited a parallel decreasing trend, peaking at a maximum value of 135.0 in 2024 and subsequently falling to a minimum value of 95.0 in 2025. This strong correlation suggests that as internal washery downtime decreases and facilities operate more reliably, the acute market demand for alternative or outsourced toll processing also diminishes, leading to a temporary stabilization of the supply chain. Such significant reductions in raw supply, whether stemming from primary mine closures or subsequent washery shutdowns, create immediate upward pressure on coal prices by constricting overall availability and increasing competition for alternative sources among global importers [54] . For Veralogix Plant Operations, these intersecting market signals underscore the absolute necessity of maintaining agile and responsive toll processing capabilities. The convergence of declining primary production volumes [51] , shifting international capacities , and volatile pricing structures [52][53] creates a highly competitive and reactive environment. Current transport difficulties have also been exacerbated by the severe deterioration of regional freight rail services, with mining operators increasingly relying on less efficient and costlier truck transportation due to systemic problems such as poor rail maintenance, cable theft, and widespread vandalism [73] .
